articles.headline: Man City to appeal guilty verdict in Premier League breaches case
articles.description: Manchester City have until Friday to lodge an appeal against the guilty verdict handed down in their case with the Premier League and have stated publicly they intend to do so.
articles.headlineJa: マンチェスター・シティ、プレミアリーグ違反問題での有罪判決に対し控訴へ
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・シティは、プレミアリーグの規約違反問題で下された有罪判決に対して金曜日までに控訴する必要があり、控訴する意向を公に表明しています。
articles.body:
Manchester City have until Friday to lodge an appeal against the guilty verdict handed down in their case with the Premier League and have stated publicly they intend to do so.

City's guilt in relation to "all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules" between 2009 and 2018 was detailed in a bombshell statement from the Premier League on Tuesday along with an accompanying written judgement from the independent commission which heard the case.

The Premier League said the "issue of sanction will be addressed separately in a further hearing with the independent commission."

In a statement issued on Tuesday, City said they will appeal the verdict.

It read: "Manchester City FC will now pursue the appeal avenues open to it, on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe."

In a video message sent out to club employees after the publication of the verdict, CEO Ferran Soriano reiterated City's intention to fight on.

"The whole Premier League case against us is based on a single false accusation," said Soriano.

"That the owner's personal money was somehow and secretly put into the club via some sponsors from Abu Dhabi. This is just not true.

"Our lawyers will now file an appeal that sets out that the opinion contains clear material errors of law, principle and fact and is unsafe."

City have the right to appeal under Premier League rules, although the competition's statement on Tuesday made clear that they want a quick resolution after initially announcing charges against City in February 2023.

"The club has the right to appeal the independent Commission's findings and has until Friday, October 2 to exercise that right," the Premier League said in their lengthy statement on Tuesday. "The Premier League Board's intention is that the full process (including any appeals and publication of relevant decisions) is concluded as soon as possible."

articles.headline: Christian Izien stars in strong defensive week for NFL stars with Africa ties
articles.description: Detroit Lions safety Christian Izien - who is from Far Rockaway, Queens, but has always proudly represented Nigeria too - was a standout among many NFL stars with ties to Africa who shone in Week 3.
articles.headlineJa: アフリカにルーツを持つNFLスターが守備で躍動した週、クリスチャン・イジエンが大活躍
articles.descriptionJa: クイーンズのファー・ロッカウェイ出身ながら誇りを持ってナイジェリアも代表するデトロイト・ライオンズのセーフティ、クリスチャン・イジエンは、第3週に輝きを放ったアフリカにゆかりのある多くのNFLスターの中でも特に目立つ活躍を見せました。
articles.body:
Detroit Lions safety Christian Izien - who is from Far Rockaway, Queens, but has always proudly represented Nigeria too - was a standout among many NFL stars with ties to Africa who shone in Week 3.

There were some highlights on offense too - notably from Jaxon Smith-Njigba and John Metchie III - but generally, this was a week where defense shone brightest for the continent's stars.

Africa Player of the Week: Christian Izien (Detroit Lions)

Izien was immensely influential for the Detroit Lions in their 31-24 win over the New York Jets, making a total of 11 tackles - nine of which were solo tackles - and defending one pass.

Izien - who has family ties to Nigeria - made three tackles for loss in addition to a vital intervention to prevent a touchdown right on the stroke of half-time. Geno Smith went for a Hail Mary with the Jets 10-7 down, but amid a sea of bodies from both teams, it was Izien who got to the ball first to tip it away.

His performance played a key role in the game ending in favour of the Lions - who are 2-1 for the season, with the Jets 1-2.

Africa Moment of the Week: Thomas Incoom and Maema Njongmeta (Carolina Panthers)

There were plenty of big hits to choose from among Africa's NFL stars. However, Incoom (born in Ghana) and Njongmeta (born in Cameroon) get the nod for collaborating in a moment which demonstrated what Africa has to offer the NFL.

As their Carolina Panthers faced the Cleveland Browns, Njongmeta forced a fumble with a huge hit on Malachi Corley and then Incoom - who had earlier set the tone with a massive hit himself - was on hand for the fumble recovery.

Although the Browns ultimately emerged victorious 21-18, it was not for any want of trying from the West African duo.

Honorable mentions

Jaxon Smith-Njigba - who proudly represents Sierra Leone, with which he has ties through his grandparents - scored two touchdowns among a total of 10 receptions for 128 yards. His Seattle Seahawks lost 33-31 to the Washington Commanders despite his contribution on offense and Uchenna Nwosu (ties to Nigeria) defending a pass.

John Metchie III - who is of Nigerian and Taiwanese descent and lived in Ghana as a young child - scored a touchdown for the Panthers in their defeat to the Browns. Nigerian-American outside linebacker Princely Umanmielen also made a notable contribution even in defeat for the Panthers, picking up a sack.

Adetomiwa Adebawore deserves special mention for his 1.5 sacks for the Indianapolis Colts in their 19-17 win over the Houston Texans.

Ruke Orhorhoro (Jacksonville Jaguars), Ogbo Okoronkwo (San Francisco 49ers), Eyioma Uwazurike (Denver Broncos), and Dayo Odeyingbo (Chicago Bears) - all of Nigerian descent - all picked up sacks in Week 3 wins.

Osa Odighizuwa, who contributed to the Niners' 36-30 win over the Arizona Cardinals with a pass defended, also has ties to Nigeria.

So, too, do players who had impressive moments on both sides of the Buffalo Bills' 24-16 win over the LA Chargers - Davison

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Real Madrid eye Van Dijk on free transfer at end of season
articles.description: Real Madrid are hoping they can sign Virgil van Dijk when his Liverpool contract expires at the end of the season. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.headlineJa: 移籍の噂・最新情報：レアル・マドリードが今季終了時にフリーでファン・ダイク獲得を狙う
articles.descriptionJa: レアル・マドリードは、今シーズン終了時にリヴァプールとの契約が満了するフィルジル・ファン・ダイクの獲得を望んでいる。「Transfer Talk」が最新情報をお届け。
articles.body:
Real Madrid are hoping they can sign Virgil van Dijk when his Liverpool contract expires at the end of the season. Plus, Gilberto Mora is subject to interest from Liverpool.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Liverpool skipper Virgil van Dijk could join Real Madrid on a free transfer when his contract expires at the end of the 2026-27 season, according to Mundo Deportivo. The 35-year-old central defender has not received an offer of a renewal from Liverpool officials, suggesting that his time at the club could be coming to a natural conclusion. Madrid boss Jose Mourinho, who already has Van Dijk's former teammates Trent Alexander-Arnold and Ibrahima Konaté in his defensive ranks, both also signed at the end of their Liverpool contracts, is interested in adding another center back. However, Madrid are not the only club monitoring the situation, with AC Milan, Galatasaray and Inter Miami also mentioned as potential destinations. Van Dijk joined Liverpool in 2018 and helped transform the club's fortunes, playing his part in the club winning every domestic trophy as well as the UEFA Champions League, UEFA Super Cup and FIFA World Club Cup.

- Liverpool are interested in Club Tijuana and Mexico international midfielder Gilberto Mora, according to Football Insider. The Reds are said to be admirers of the 17-year-old, but there is significant competition emerging in the race for his signature, with Real Madrid, Barcelona, and Paris Saint-Germain also keen. The Liga MX side are expected to part ways with him at the end of the season when they believe his value will be at its highest. Mora impressed at the World Cup in the summer and has made an impressive start to the new campaign with five goals in seven matches.

- Real Madrid are monitoring the situation of Manchester City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma, TEAMtalk reports. Madrid are assessing the transfer market for a long-term option between the posts, and they see the 27-year-old as a strong candidate to succeed Thibaut Courtois due to his experience in the Champions League. Whether City part ways with Donnarumma could hinge on their punishment after they were found guilty on Tuesday of almost all 115 financial charges brought against them by the Premier League. City have until Friday to appeal.

- Barcelona defender Jules Koundé has been placed on the shortlist of Bayern Munich, Diario Sport reports. The Bundesliga club have kept close tabs on the 27-year-old for some time, and they are lining up an approach for him as a potential future successor to defender Kim Min-jae. Kounde signed a new five-year contract back in August 2025, but having failed to establish himself as a starter in La Liga this season, a switch to the Allianz Arena could become a possibility in the January transfer window.

articles.headline: Which Premier League players got injured in the international break?
articles.description: All the latest news and updates on Premier League stars injuries during the first international break of the 2026-2027 club season
articles.headlineJa: 代表ウィークで負傷したプレミアリーグの選手は？
articles.descriptionJa: 2026-2027クラブシーズンの最初の代表ウィーク中に発生した、プレミアリーグのスター選手たちの負傷に関する最新ニュースと更新情報。
articles.body:
Premier League teams will be watching and hoping their star players remain healthy throughout the international break.

However, some have already sustained injuries while playing for their countries. Premier League matches resume on Oct. 10.

ESPN will be tracking the latest injuries and updates for your club's players:

Kai Havertz (Arsenal)

Arsenal's Kai Havertz was forced off in the 30th minute of the game between Netherlands and Germany on September 24th with what was described as a muscle injury.

"Both are currently undergoing an MRI," Jurgen Klopp said on RTL about Havertz and Jamal Musiala. "I hope we get the diagnosis [on Thursday] evening. But of course, this isn't great. I hope it's nothing serious. The lads are probably out for us. But hopefully, they'll be back in action relatively quickly."

On September 25 the German Football Association confirmed the attacker would be leaving Klopp's camp and return to Arsenal after suffering what they describe as a 'muscle strain.'

Brian Brobbey (Sunderland)

The powerful Sunderland attacker was also injured in the same game after picking up what looked like a hamstring injury while running for the ball. He immediately went down and signalled to the sideline.

He left the field of his own accord but did have a heavy limp as he walked down the tunnel.

Netherlands boss Xavi Hernandez said after the game: "Brian is indeed injured."

Brobbey was replaced by Joshua Zirkzee in the Dutch squad.

Zion Suzuki (Aston Villa)

The goalkeeper linked up with the Japan squad but according to reports missed the main group training session on September 22nd, according to local reports. Instead he was put on an individual session for a rib injury.

Suzuki was subsequently left out of Japan's matchday squad entirely for Thursday's 3-1 victory over Uruguay.

Dan Ballard (Sunderland)

The Sunderland defender suffered a reported hamstring injury during Northern Ireland's 1-0 victory over Georgia in the UEFA Nations League.

With the score still 0-0 as the match moved into stoppage time, Ballard chased back as Georgia counter-attacked and pulled up clutching the back of his thigh, unable to finish the match in Tbilisi.

Speaking immediately after Friday's match, manager Michael O'Neill said it was too soon to know the extent of his latest injury but will definitely miss the next three Northern Ireland games.

"We'll scan him tomorrow (Saturday), but he's certainly not going to be available for the next three games."

Alexander Isak (Liverpool)

Alexander Isak is returning to Liverpool after sustaining a "minor injury" on international duty.

The striker scored and played the full 90 minutes in Sweden's 2-1 victory over Romania in the Nations League on Friday.

But Isak, who has made a strong start to the season for Liverpool, will not feature in matches against Poland, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Romania over the remainder of the extended international break.

articles.headline: Liverpool can't afford to be without Isak, Gakpo ahead of daunting October fixture list
articles.description: Between them, Cody Gakpo and Alexander Isak have scored five of Liverpool's seven league goals this season so their injuries during the international break could prove costly.
articles.headlineJa: 過酷な10月の日程を控えるリヴァプール、イサクとガクポの離脱は許されない状況に
articles.descriptionJa: コーディ・ガクポとアレクサンダー・イサクの2人は今季リヴァプールが記録したリーグ戦7ゴールのうち5ゴールを挙げており、代表ウィーク中の負傷は大きな痛手となる可能性がある。
articles.body:
"Clearly there's not another Alexander Isak, that's obvious." That was the admission of Sweden boss Graham Potter after confirming the Liverpool striker had been forced to withdraw from international duty over the weekend with a minor thigh injury.

"In an ideal world, we want all our players available, but the reality is we don't have Alex for this game," Potter added, ahead of Sweden's 3-1 victory over Poland on Monday night. "Clearly whoever comes in, we're not going to ask them to be Alex. They just need to be themselves in the best way they can."

Potter's frustration at losing Isak for Sweden's upcoming UEFA Nations League games is reflective of the forward's growing importance for both club and country.

A cocktail of poor form and fitness saw the 27-year-old relegated to a largely peripheral figure last term following his British-record £125 million transfer from Newcastle United to Liverpool in summer 2025. However, in the early weeks of the new campaign, Isak has managed to recapture his prolific edge in front of goal, netting five times in eight appearances for Liverpool and Sweden. It makes the prospect of his potential injury layoff all the more concerning for the Reds, who face a punishing schedule of nine games in 29 days upon their return from the international break.

That fellow in-form forward Cody Gakpo has also been forced to return to Liverpool with an ankle problem sustained while playing for Netherlands only compounds the need for Isak to be fit and firing in time for Oct. 11, when Andoni Iraola's side host Manchester City in the Premier League.

Having waited so long for his Anfield career to spark into life, the Sweden international will know better than anyone that he can ill-afford his fine start to the season to be derailed by another injury setback.

"If Alex is fit, he will produce the numbers"

Isak's latest goal for Liverpool felt like a moment of catharsis. After scoring what turned out to be the winner in the Reds' 1-0 victory over AFC Bournemouth on Sept. 20, the striker charged into the away end at the Vitality Stadium -- even earning himself a yellow card for his troubles.

His beaming smile as he celebrated with the travelling Liverpool supporters, though, suggested that he didn't care a jot. Renowned for his composed -- sometimes aloof -- demeanor, Isak's obvious delight on the south coast was indicative of a player who is increasingly beginning to feel like he belongs at Anfield. It is a marked departure from last season, when his early struggles for fitness and subsequent leg fracture left him watching much of the action from the sidelines.

Already this term, the striker's tally of four Premier League goals has surpassed his entire haul from last season (three). articles.headline: Roy Keane: I'd put Man City medals 'in the bin' after 'cheating'
articles.description: Roy Keane has said if he was a Manchester City player he would put his medals "in the bin" following the Premier League's ruling that the club was guilty of breaching over 100 financial regulations.
articles.headlineJa: ロイ・キーン氏：「不正行為」発覚ならマンCのメダルは「ゴミ箱に捨てる」
articles.descriptionJa: プレミアリーグがマンチェスター・シティに対し100件以上の財務規則違反で有罪の裁定を下したことを受け、ロイ・キーン氏は自身がマンチェスター・シティの選手であればメダルを「ゴミ箱に捨てる」と語った。
articles.body:
Roy Keane has said if he was a Manchester City player he would put his medals "in the bin" following the Premier League's ruling that the club was guilty of breaching over 100 financial regulations.

On Tuesday, the Premier League confirmed City had been found guilty of inflating the club's commercial revenue by £830 million ($1.08 billion) between 2009 and 2018.

Premier League CEO Richard Masters said the club had "systematically broke Premier League rules for nearly a decade."

Former Manchester United legend Keane said he would not hold on to any of the medals he'd won if he was a City player.

"If I was a player, I'd be 100% sticking those medals in the bin. Of course you would, it's cheating," Keane told ITV Sport. "They won it on the pitch because cheating was going on.

"They knew it would hurt a lot of people, but they've still done it."

City deny any wrongdoing and said they were "surprised" by the ruling. They have until Friday, Oct. 2 to appeal the verdict.

During the period between 2009-18, the club won three Premier League titles, an FA Cup and three League Cup titles.

- Sources: Man City learned of guilty verdicts in summer before transfer activity

In a video to staff, City CEO Ferran Soriano said the outcome was the result of a "Premier League conspiracy theory."

"This has gone on for so long that it's important to remind ourselves that the whole Premier League case against us is based on a single false accusation; that the owner's personal money was somehow and secretly put into the club via some sponsors from Abu Dhabi," he said.

articles.headline: NBA issues new guidelines, instructs refs to crack down on push-offs
articles.description: The NBA has issued new guidance to its referees on four types of "high-volume and highly impactful" calls, including push-offs.
articles.headlineJa: NBAが新ガイドラインを発表、審判にプッシュオフの厳格な取り締まりを指示
articles.descriptionJa: NBAは審判に対し、プッシュオフを含む「発生頻度が高く、影響の大きい」4種類のファウル判定に関する新たな指導を行いました。
articles.body:
The NBA has instructed its referees to crack down on offensive players who use their arms to push off against defensive players during the upcoming season, one of several new points of emphasis for officials, the league announced on a conference call Tuesday.

James Jones, the NBA's executive vice president of basketball operations, said the league has issued new guidance on four types of "high-volume and highly impactful" calls, including push-offs. The NBA's goal, James said, is to ensure that "the way our game is played, and the way our game presents, continues to track favorably" for players and fans.

A push-off most commonly occurs when an offensive player uses his non-dribbling arm to contact a defensive player so that he can create space to attempt a shot from the perimeter. While some level of jockeying between offensive players and defensive players is legal and to be expected, the NBA's referees will now use the "Four F's" framework to determine if they should call an offensive foul on a push off:

The "Four F's" are feeling, firming, force and full extension.

Referees have been instructed that a ball handler is allowed to use his off arm to "feel" his opponent or to "firm up" by gathering himself in front of a defensive player. However, referees should assess an offensive foul if the ball handler's off arm contacts the defender with "force" or is "fully extended" to create an advantage.

"We've got to make sure the defensive side of the ball does not get penalized by allowing illegal acts by the offensive player," said Monty McCutchen, the NBA's senior vice president of referee development and training. "I think we can do a better job."

The new guidance on push-offs comes during the middle of an ongoing scoring boom: NBA teams averaged 115.6 points last season, the highest mark since the 1969-70 season. In recent years, the NBA has sought to cut down on other illegal actions by offensive players, such as stopping short to create collisions, splaying legs during shot attempts and jumping sideways into defenders to draw free throws.

Michael Jordan authored perhaps the most famous push-off in NBA history when he freed himself from Utah Jazz guard Bryon Russell for a midrange jumper in the closing seconds of Game 6 of the 1998 NBA Finals. No offensive foul was called, Jordan made the shot and the Bulls won their sixth championship of the 1990s.

By the NBA's new "Four F's" standard, Jordan wouldn't be whistled for an offensive foul against Russell because he didn't contact Russell's body with noticeable "force" or fully extend his left arm.

The NBA released a video Tuesday featuring several push-offs that it would deem to be offensive fouls under its new framework. In one clip, then-Boston Celtics star Jaylen Brown raised his right forearm and shoved into the chest of then-Philadelphia 76ers forward Kelly Oubre Jr. to set up a jumper near the free throw line.

articles.headline: Ravens-Cowboys in Brazil averaged record 24.9M viewers
articles.description: The Ravens' 34-31 victory over the Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, averaged 24.9 million viewers on CBS on Sunday, making it the most-watched NFL international game in history.
articles.headlineJa: ブラジルでのレイブンズ対カウボーイズ戦、平均視聴者数2490万人の新記録を達成
articles.descriptionJa: ブラジルのリオデジャネイロで行われ、レイブンズがカウボーイズに34-31で勝利した日曜日の試合はCBSで平均2490万人が視聴し、NFLの国際試合として史上最多の視聴者数を記録しました。
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- The Ravens' 34-31 victory over the Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, averaged 24.9 million viewers on CBS on Sunday, making it the most-watched NFL international game in history.

According to Nielsen, the audience peaked to more than 30 million during the late stages when Baltimore's Tyler Loop made a 56-yard field goal on the last play. It also was the most-watched Week 3 game on CBS since 2014.

This year's Week 1 game in Australia between the San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams averaged 18.5 million in the U.S. on Netflix. Last year's Week 1 Friday night game in Brazil between the Los Angeles Chargers and Kansas City Chiefs also averaged 18.5 million on YouTube.

Sunday's CBS doubleheader averaged 21.45 million, its most-watched September doubleheader since 2014.

The other six international games last year were on NFL Network and averaged 6.2 million.

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

articles.headline: Kessler talks up Lakers' title hopes behind 'nasty' defense
articles.description: New addition Walker Kessler is convinced the Lakers have the right guys to be "a nasty defensive team" and a contender in the Western Conference this season.
articles.headlineJa: ケスラー、「エグい」守備を武器にレイカーズの優勝への期待を語る
articles.descriptionJa: 新加入のウォーカー・ケスラーは、今季のレイカーズには「強力でエグい守備チーム」となり、ウェスタン・カンファレンスの優勝争いに加わるための適切なメンバーが揃っていると確信しています。
articles.body:
EL SEGUNDO, Calif. -- The Los Angeles Lakers' offense has thrived since Luka Doncic arrived in 2025, but center Walker Kessler needed only one day of training camp to be convinced the team's defense will hold up its end of the bargain this season.

"Listen, I think we're going to be a nasty defensive team," Kessler said Tuesday. "I think people aren't taking into account how good our perimeter defense is going to be. A lot of guys are very smart on the perimeter and positionally can play really good defense. We have guys who are just ball hawks."

During JJ Redick's two seasons as coach, the Lakers have ranked above average in offensive efficiency and below average in defensive efficiency. After a transformative summer that saw the departure of LeBron James and several other veteran players, the Lakers are hoping to establish a more aggressive defensive identity with a rebuilt roster that includes Doncic, guard Austin Reaves, Kessler and a deep group of young wings.

Redick said Tuesday that his first goal during training camp was to "establish our defensive principles." With both forward spots in the starting lineup open for competition, Redick said he met with the team's wings last week to give them their marching orders.

"They understood the assignment today," he said. "That was exciting. They set the tone for us defensively. There was a lot of physicality, a lot of grabbing and holding, and a lot of disruption without gambling."

The 7-foot-2 Kessler, who was traded by the Utah Jazz to the Lakers this summer, will serve as the back-line rim protector after averaging 2.4 blocks per game during his first four seasons.

"The paint is kind of closed when [Kessler] is on the court," Doncic said.

From there, Doncic's remade supporting cast includes defensive specialists Jarred Vanderbilt and Matisse Thybulle as well as free agent additions Quentin Grimes, Sandro Mamukelashvili, Collin Sexton and Ziaire Williams. Kevon Looney, a veteran center who won two championships with the Golden State Warriors, will back up Kessler.

Kessler praised Looney for his "mind and positioning," Vanderbilt for his skill defending all five positions, and Thybulle, Grimes, Sexton and Williams for their ability to apply defensive pressure.

"Having those guys that can steal the ball ... [and] when they do get beat, be able to recover, it makes my job a lot easier," he said. "It's a lot easier to block a shot when a dude has someone on his hip instead of an open lane towards the basket."

The Lakers boasted the NBA's No. 3 defense when they won the 2020 championship and the No. 1 defense during the 2020-21 regular season. But their performance on that end has slipped noticeably in the years that followed.

articles.headline: Steelers' Ramsey says he has broken wrist, uncertain for Thursday
articles.description: Steelers cornerback Jalen Ramsey said he would "try" to play Thursday night against the Browns despite saying he broke his wrist in the team's Week 3 win.
articles.headlineJa: スティーラーズのラムジー、手首骨折を明かす　木曜日の試合出場は不透明
articles.descriptionJa: スティーラーズのコーナーバック（CB）ジェイレン・ラムジーは、第3週の勝利で手首を骨折したと明かしたものの、木曜夜のブラウンズ戦には出場を「試みる」と語りました。

articles.headline: Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy: Man City verdict could lead to Premier League expulsion
articles.description: Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy has said Manchester City could be thrown out of the Premier League after being found guilty of all charges of financial breaches by an independent commission.
articles.headlineJa: リサ・ナンディ文化相：マンCへの有罪判決によりプレミアリーグ追放の可能性も
articles.descriptionJa: リサ・ナンディ文化相は、マンチェスター・シティが独立委員会によって財務違反の全容疑で有罪判決を受けたことを受け、プレミアリーグから追放される可能性があると述べました。

articles.headline: Ex-NBA champ JR Smith arrested on assault charge in Texas
articles.description: Former NBA champion JR Smith was arrested Monday in Texas on a charge of assault causing "bodily injury family violence."
articles.headlineJa: 元NBA王者のJR・スミス、テキサス州で暴行容疑により逮捕
articles.descriptionJa: 元NBA王者のJR・スミスが月曜日、「身体的危害を伴う家庭内暴力」の暴行容疑でテキサス州にて逮捕されました。

articles.headline: PSG chief Al-Khelaifi has 'zero interest' in FIFA presidency
articles.description: European soccer's search for a candidate to challenge Gianni Infantino in the FIFA presidential election will not land on clubs' leader Nasser Al-Khelaifi.

articles.descriptionJa: FIFA会長選でジャンニ・インファンティーノに挑む候補者を模索している欧州サッカー界ですが、欧州クラブ協会のトップであるナセル・アル・ケライフィが立候補することはありません。

articles.headline: Knicks still undecided if they will visit White House
articles.description: The Knicks are still deciding if they will become the first NBA champions to visit the White House under President Donald Trump.
